I've worked on CanSat-related projects involving ESP32, sensors, imaging, and ground-station development, and I'm excited to apply my engineering background to a real-world Earth observation challenge.
summary:
EARTHBEAT is a cross-platform application that explores surface dynamics across the Indus Delta in Sindh, Pakistan, using NASA–ISRO NISAR satellite observations. It brings together 10 radar acquisitions from July to November 2026, enabling users to browse observations and explore dual- and quad-polarization imaging on web and mobile devices.

Our project attempts to investigates how river discharge, rainfall, and coastal water levels may influence surface-water extent and persistence across the lower Indus Delta. With an interactive interface, Python FastAPI backend, and an analytical framework for exploring polarization, backscatter, and surface change, EARTHBEAT makes satellite observations more accessible and promotes understanding of environmental changes in a climate-vulnerable region.
details:
EARTHBEAT (The Changing Pulse of Earth's Surface)

Project Overview

EARTHBEAT is a cross-platform application that makes NASA–ISRO NISAR satellite observations accessible through an interactive visualization platform. Our project focuses on the Indus Delta in Sindh, Pakistan, a climate-vulnerable coastal region affected by changing environmental and hydrological conditions.

The application brings together 10 NISAR radar acquisitions collected between July and November 2026. Users can browse observations by acquisition date, view satellite image previews, and explore the differences between dual-polarization and quad-polarization imaging.

How It Works

EARTHBEAT uses a React Native and Expo frontend to support both web and mobile devices. A Python FastAPI backend serves the satellite observation catalogue and corresponding image previews through REST API endpoints.

The interface organizes the available acquisitions chronologically and presents information about their dates, polarization configurations, and study region. It also introduces users to key concepts associated with SAR remote sensing, including radar polarization, backscatter, and surface-change monitoring.

The current version focuses on data accessibility, visualization, and scientific exploration rather than performing quantitative satellite-image analysis.

Benefits and Intended Impact

EARTHBEAT lowers the barrier to exploring satellite observations by presenting them through a simple, accessible interface rather than requiring users to navigate complex scientific data products independently.

By focusing on the Indus Delta, it connects Earth-observation technology to a relevant environmental context in Pakistan and encourages further investigation into coastal dynamics, surface-water changes, and environmental monitoring.

Tools and Technologies

  • Frontend: React Native, Expo, TypeScript
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI
  • Communication: REST APIs
  • Satellite Data: NASA–ISRO NISAR radar observation browse products
  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code, Git, GitHub

Creativity and Design Considerations

EARTHBEAT combines a geographically focused environmental question with a cross-platform satellite-observation viewer. Its chronological browsing experience allows users to explore multiple acquisitions of the same study region and understand how satellite observations can contribute to environmental monitoring.

During development, we considered data accessibility, geographic coverage, acquisition dates, polarization configurations, application performance, and usability across web and mobile devices. We also accounted for the limitations of browse imagery, avoiding claims of quantitative measurements that require calibrated satellite data processing.

EARTHBEAT provides an accessible starting point for exploring NISAR observations and demonstrates how complex Earth-observation datasets can be presented through a practical, user-friendly application.
